settings.title: Settings
settings.language.hint: Interface, menus and notifications. Changing it reloads the window.
settings.general.followUp: Message sent while the agent is working
settings.general.followUp.hint: Queue: waits for the turn to end. Steer: joins the turn in progress.
settings.general.noCollapse.hint: Shows every tool call and intermediate message
settings.general.notifications.hint: When an agent finishes or asks for permission while the app is in the background
settings.general.resources: Show resource usage in the sidebar
settings.general.resources.hint: Memory and CPU for Kabul and its agents; click for details
settings.general.caffeinate: Keep the Mac awake while agents run
settings.general.caffeinate.hint: Uses caffeinate while a session is active
settings.general.tray.hint: AI limits and spend, running agents and quick actions (system tray on Windows)
settings.general.alertPct.hint: Notifies when a usage window (5 h, week, month) goes past this
settings.general.budget.hint: Warns at 80% and 100%; only counts the cost the agent reports
settings.general.codexbar.hint: Limits for more providers, status and credits via the CodexBar CLI (optional)
settings.general.context.hint: Otherwise the ring only shows above 70%
settings.general.longText: Turn long text into an attachment
settings.general.longText.hint: Pasting more than 5,000 characters creates a file in .context/attachments
settings.general.absolutelyRight.hint: Strips the phrase from the start of replies
settings.appearance.lead: Interface theme. “System” follows the macOS appearance. ⌥⌘T toggles it; also in ⌘K.
settings.appearance.zoom.hint: ⌘+ zooms in, ⌘− zooms out, ⌘0 resets to 100%
settings.appearance.contrast.hint: Background and text closer together in the dark theme
settings.appearance.cb.hint: Replaces green/red in diffs and statuses
settings.appearance.termSize.hint: 10 to 20 px; applies to terminals opened afterwards
settings.appearance.bigTerm.hint: The command runs as soon as the tab opens, in the workspace's worktree
settings.models.codexPersonality.hint: Saved; the installed Codex doesn't confirm this option yet
settings.models.review.hint: The Review button (⌘⇧R) opens a new chat with this model
settings.models.agySkip.hint: Off (default): every Gemini (agy) command or write asks for approval in a card, and the approved rule only applies to this workspace. On: the agent runs any command and writes any file without asking. Applies to new chats.
settings.models.agySkip.confirm: Approve everything automatically in Gemini? The agent will run commands and change files without asking. Only use this in repositories you trust.
settings.env.userLead: Passed to agents, scripts and terminals. Scope “all” or one agent (claude, codex, opencode, qwen, gemini, agy). E.g. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, HTTPS_PROXY.
settings.env.repoLead: Apply to this repository's workspaces. Those from the shared repository ({shared}, versioned) show as inherited; yours live in {local} and override them.
settings.repo.label: Repository
settings.actions.lead: Instructions appended to each action's prompt in this repository. “General preferences” also go to Claude as a system instruction.
settings.actions.generalPlaceholder: e.g. Reply in English; run the tests before saying you're done.
settings.misc.icon.hint: Shown in the sidebar instead of the initial
settings.misc.preview.hint: $KABUL_PORT and $((KABUL_PORT+1)) become the workspace's port (⌘⇧B in the terminal opens localhost)
settings.misc.remove.hint: Removes it from Kabul; the folder stays on disk. Its workspaces must be archived.
settings.advanced.scrollback.hint: In MB; applies to terminals opened afterwards
settings.accounts.lead: Sign-in uses each CLI's own flow. Kabul only shows the URL and passes the code along; tokens are never read.
settings.accounts.installConfirm: Install {name}? The command runs in a tmux session visible in the Dashboard.
settings.repo.setup.hint: runs when the workspace is created, with the KABUL_* variables (KABUL_PORT, KABUL_WORKSPACE_PATH…)
settings.repo.include: Ignored files to copy into each worktree
settings.shortcuts.needModifier: Use ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ together with the key.
settings.shortcuts.recordTitle: Click and type the new shortcut (Esc cancels)
settings.linear.lead: Create workspaces from issues, @mention issues in chat and link the PR to the issue. The key is stored in the macOS Keychain.
settings.linear.generate: Generate a key in Linear › Settings › Security ↗
settings.linear.oauth: Linear OAuth: pending (requires registering the Kabul app with Linear); a personal key gives the same read access to issues.
settings.github.tokenSaved: Personal token saved in the Keychain
settings.machines.lead: Each machine runs {kabuld} and shows up in the picker at the top of the sidebar (⌃1…⌃9). Use the Tailscale address, for example {example}. Switching machines switches where repositories and workspaces come from.
settings.machines.name: Name (e.g. Office Mac)
settings.accounts.removeConfirm: Remove the account "{name}"? Its credentials in Kabul are deleted.
settings.accounts.nickname: Nickname for the new {provider} account (e.g. Work)
settings.login.timedOut: Time to paste the code ran out. Try again.
settings.login.expired: The link expired; generating a new one…
settings.remote.lead: {kabuld} lets your phone (and your other machines) watch and drive every session on this computer live. It only listens on this computer and on your Tailscale network; nothing is exposed to the internet.
settings.remote.netOff: Off on this kabuld: only this computer has access.
settings.remote.pairLead: On your phone (connected to the same Tailscale), point the camera at the QR code. The code is valid for 5 minutes and works once; the device gets its own credential, which you can revoke below.
settings.remote.inviteNeedsWs: Create a workspace to invite someone.
settings.remote.inviteLead: The person needs to be on your tailnet (share the machine via Tailscale). They see the workspace's stream, chat and terminal; as an editor, they can also send messages, approve and type. Everything goes through the server's single queue, labeled with who wrote it.
settings.remote.machineAdded: {name} added: pick it in the selector at the top of the sidebar.
settings.remote.otherLead: Every machine with kabuld on shows up in the selector at the top of the sidebar, and you drive it from the same app. To add one: on that machine, open this screen and copy the QR link; paste it here.
settings.remote.pairLink: Pairing link from the other machine
settings.https.title: HTTPS via Tailscale
settings.https.lead: On iPhone, installing Kabul on the Home Screen (PWA), getting notifications and using the microphone for dictation {required}. Without HTTPS, the phone opens {http}: the list, terminal and chat work, the rest doesn't. Kabul uses {serve}, which is only visible on your tailnet.
settings.https.qrUses: The pairing QR code below already uses this address.
settings.https.offNote: Turning it off removes the port 443 rule from tailscale serve.
settings.https.missing: HTTPS isn't enabled on your tailnet yet
settings.https.step1: Open the Tailscale DNS admin page: {link}
settings.https.noChange: Kabul doesn't change your tailnet's configuration: you do that in the admin panel.
settings.https.stillOff: Checked again: the tailnet still isn't enabled for HTTPS.
settings.updates.auto.hint: Checks for a new version when the app opens and shows a notice at the top; installing only happens when you confirm
settings.updates.channel.hint: Beta gets test versions early (and stable ones too)
settings.updates.title: Kabul updates
settings.updates.errorHint: You can also download versions from the

settings.updates.waiting.one: Waiting for 1 agent to finish; Kabul will update and restart right after.
settings.updates.waiting.other: Waiting for {count} agents to finish; Kabul will update and restart right after.

settings.updates.agentsRunning.one: Updating restarts Kabul, and 1 agent is running.
settings.updates.agentsRunning.other: Updating restarts Kabul, and {count} agents are running.

settings.updates.agentsStop: Restarting now stops them mid-task. If you wait, Kabul updates on its own when they finish.
settings.local.pullConfirm: Download "{model}" via {source}? It can take up several GB. The download runs in a tmux session visible in the Dashboard.
settings.local.title: Local models
settings.local.addEndpoint: Add endpoint (OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible, local or on another machine)
settings.local.name: Name
settings.local.bestHarnessLead: For each family, Kabul uses the first installed harness that speaks one of the endpoint's APIs; the others are fallbacks.
settings.diag.title: Diagnostics
settings.general.trayIcon.hint: What the icon shows: the tightest limits or up to 3 you choose, the style and today's spend
